Correction
kuh-REK-shun
noun
From the Hebrew musar, “discipline, chastening,” and the Greek epanorth&omacr;sis, “a setting straight again,” the reproof and chastening of the LORD and of His Word.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

📖 Biblical Definition

Correction is the reproof and chastening by which the LORD and His Word set the erring straight and bring the wandering back into the way. The Scripture names it among the great profits of the inspired Word: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works (2Ti 3:16). It is therefore no harsh or alien thing, but a means of the LORD’s love, and Solomon binds the son not to despise it: My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction: for whom the LORD loveth he correcteth (Pro 3:11-12). Folly is bound in the heart of a child, but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him (Pro 22:15). The Hebrews take up the same theme, that the LORD chasteneth every son whom He receiveth, and that no chastening for the present seemeth joyous, but grievous; nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby (Heb 12:6-11). The dictionary marks that correction is the LORD’s fatherly dealing, not His wrath, the proof of sonship and not its denial. He who is left uncorrected is no son but a bastard; but the child whom God reproves by His Word and chastens by His hand is made partaker of His holiness, and shall reap the peaceable fruit thereof.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The reproof and chastening of the LORD and His Word, profitable to make the man of God perfect.

CORRECTION, the reproof and chastening that sets the erring straight.

It is named a profit of the inspired Word, to perfect the man of God.

📖 Key Scripture

2Ti 3:16 — "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:"

Pro 3:11 — "My son, despise not the chastening of the LORD; neither be weary of his correction:"

Pro 22:15 — "Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child; but the rod of correction shall drive it far from him."

Heb 12:6 — "For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The present age rejects all correction and discipline as harmful, and would strip from the Word and the family the LORD’s loving chastening.

expand to see more

The spirit of the age has set itself against correction in every form, naming all reproof and discipline as harmful, and bidding men affirm what is in them rather than reprove it. The Word that is profitable for reproof and correction is recast as too sharp for tender hearts; the rod that drives folly from a child is forbidden; the chastening hand of the heavenly Father is mistaken for cruelty. So a whole generation is taught to despise the very thing the Scripture calls the proof of a Father’s love, and to flee from the discipline that alone can make the wandering wise.

The dictionary answers in the plain words of Scripture, not in the borrowed speech of the age. Correction is the LORD’s fatherly dealing with His own; whom He loveth He chasteneth, and scourgeth every son He receiveth, and the child left uncorrected is no true son but a bastard. No chastening seemeth joyous for the present, but grievous; yet afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness to them that are exercised thereby. The recovery is to despise not the chastening of the LORD, to receive His reproof as love and not as cruelty, and to submit son and self alike to the correcting Word that the man of God may be perfect.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “chastening” and the Greek for “a setting straight,” correction names the LORD’s loving reproof of His own.

Correction — Hebrew musar, “discipline, chastening.”

The Greek epanorth&omacr;sis means “a setting straight again.”

All Scripture is profitable for reproof and for correction.

The rod of correction drives folly from the heart of a child.

The LORD chasteneth every son whom He receiveth, in love.
